headline: Advances in Quantum Fault Tolerance and Processing
summary: Today's research spans significant theoretical developments in adversarial fault tolerance for both classical and quantum architectures, alongside new insights into quantum state metrology, chaotic spectra, and high-rate neutral-atom hardware.

themes.title: Adversarial Fault-Tolerance in Circuits
themes.body: New techniques push the boundaries of circuit robustness against worst-case adversarial corruptions, introducing fault-tolerant schemes capable of handling nearly linear noise rates in both classical and quantum settings.

themes.title: Quantum States, Readout, and Metrology
themes.body: Recent works explore the spectral edge rigidity of quantum chaotic states, optimal minimax readout strategies for unknown qubit directions, and classical-limit formulas for one-dimensional potentials.

themes.title: High-Throughput Quantum Hardware
themes.body: Demonstrations of reusable neutral-atom arrays achieve high raw circuit iteration rates and improved Fisher information rates through non-destructive readout and atom retention.

connections.body: Both papers address fault tolerance against severe adversarial noise, extending error-correction and detection mechanisms to handle near-linear or global worst-case corruptions.
